name: Empire of Japan

areaKm2.note: world_1900 polygon "Imperial Japan" = 369,100 km2 on the sphere (Japan proper and Kurils, without Taiwan); official area of Japan proper ~382,000 km2.

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1905 = 46,620k (Japan proper); HYDE/Gapminder (OWID) 47.0M. Taiwan and Korea excluded.

activePersonnel.note: Russo-Japanese War infobox: Japan 1,200,000 total mobilised, 650,000 peak (in the field); plus depots at home and the navy (~45,000). Mukden (Feb-Mar 1905) ~270,000 Japanese.

trainedReserves.note: Page: 850,000 trained men available at the outbreak (active + 1st reserve 380,000, 2nd reserve 200,000, conscript reserve 50,000, kokumin 220,000), most already called by 1905; remaining kokumin and replacement drafts.

supportPersonnel.note: Artillery ~60,000, engineers, transport (hojukohei) and medical ~95,000, navy ~45,000. Reconstruction.

mobilizationRatio.note: Page: 1,200,000 mobilised in 1904-05 of ~46.6M = 2.6%, with 4,250,000 untrained men in the reserve pool.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Page: 257,000 infantry immediately available in 1904 (division 11,400 infantry); 4 new divisions and reserve brigades formed in 1904; ~65% of the field army infantry by 1905.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Arisaka Type 30 rifle, machine guns added during the war

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: 3-year conscripts; reserves had a full year of training, cut to 6 months as losses mounted (page)

count.note: Page: 11,000 cavalry at the outbreak (2 brigades plus divisional regiments, 430 per division), expanded in 1904.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: small horses

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: weakest arm, often dismounted

count.note: Page: 894 guns immediately available (Connaughton) or 1,080 field guns plus 120-150 heavy (Olender) at the outbreak; more by 1905 incl. 28 cm siege howitzers at Port Arthur.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Type 31 75 mm, not a true quick-firer

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: indirect fire used well at the Yalu

count.note: Tsushima order of battle (page): 4 battleships, 29 cruisers (incl. 8 armoured), plus the old ex-Chinese ironclad Chin'en; coast-defence ships at home.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: British-built Mikasa class, Shimose powder

training.note: Rubric row: training 1.0. Evidence: crossed the T at Tsushima, lost 3 torpedo boats against 6 Russian battleships sunk (page)

count.note: Page: 21 destroyers, 45 torpedo boats and 4 gunboats at Tsushima.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: British- and Japanese-built destroyers

training.note: Rubric row: training 1.0. Evidence: night torpedo attacks at Tsushima

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.75. Evidence: Oyama and Kodama on land, Togo at sea (best-in-era naval command)

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75-1.0. Evidence: regional regiments, frontal assaults at Port Arthur pressed despite losses

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75-1.0. Evidence: nationalist mobilisation, victories since 1894

weapons.note: Anchor: 7 (1905). Evidence: magazine rifles, machine guns, field guns

armor.note: Anchor: 7 (1905). Evidence: no armoured cars or helmets

fortification.note: Anchor: 7 (1905). Evidence: coastal forts, field trenches at Mukden

logistics.note: Anchor: 7 (1905). Evidence: sea lift to Korea and Manchuria, light field railways

communications.note: Anchor: 7 (1905). Evidence: field telephones, naval wireless (Shinano Maru report at Tsushima)

isr.note: Anchor: 7 (1905). Evidence: wireless-equipped scouting cruisers, balloons at Port Arthur

air.note: No military aircraft before 1911; balloons, where used, are counted under ISR.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: COW NMC v7 milex (thousands of pounds): 1904 = 67,273, 1905 = 73,031. Against a GNP of ~3bn yen (~300M pounds) that is ~20-25% in war; peacetime ~4-5%.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: mining and manufacturing about a fifth of output (Ohkawa estimates).

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess: rice-based agriculture, small net rice imports.

annualCohort.note: Analogue ratio of the France 1805 snapshot (~0.95% of population reaching 20 each year) applied to 46.8M.

artillery.note: Educated guess: Osaka Arsenal field-gun output per year.

ships_major.note: Educated guess: cruisers and battleships completed per year in Japanese yards (Kure, Yokosuka); battleships still bought in Britain.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: national and prefectural roads.

railKm.note: CHAT railline Japan 1904 = 5,735 km, 1905 = 5,843 km. High adds the Seoul-Busan line and military light railways in Korea and Manchuria.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: Yokosuka, Kure, Sasebo, Maizuru, Yokohama, Kobe, Osaka, Nagasaki, Moji, Ujina.

merchantTonnage.note: Registered merchant tonnage 940k tons (Japan 1905, CHAT dataset https://data.nber.org/chat/chat.dta, variable shipton_all) x 1.5 (range 1.3-1.6). CHAT tonnage is registered (largely net) tons, so this may understate deadweight.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: sea and light-rail supply in Manchuria.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: island home, coastal forts, strong population support.

notes: Snapshot = Empire of Japan in spring 1905 (Mukden, March; Tsushima, May), army on war footing. Population and territory = Japan proper; Taiwan (colony) and Korea are bases, not included; includes is empty. Personnel: mobilised army and navy = active; untapped kokumin and replacement drafts = trainedReserves. Strengths from the Russo-Japanese War page (Connaughton; Olender) and the Tsushima page. Branch split is a reconstruction (grade C).
